---
title: Scaffolding a Plugin
description: Generating a buildable plugin starter kit using wefter create-plugin and the mandatory Android package namespace rule.
---

## Overview

Use the [`wefter create-plugin`](/cli/create-plugin) CLI command to generate a buildable, cross-platform Wefter native plugin boilerplate package.

```bash
wefter create-plugin <name> [targetDir]
```

---

## Generated File Structure

Running `wefter create-plugin secure-storage` scaffolds a ready-to-build plugin directory:

```text
secure-storage/
├── package.json
├── plugin.json
├── README.md
├── src/
│   └── index.ts
├── android/
│   └── SecureStoragePlugin.kt
└── ios/
    └── SecureStoragePlugin.swift
```

---

## Dynamic Android Package Rewriting

Every Wefter plugin's Android Kotlin source code contains a package header line (e.g. `package dev.wefter.bridge` or `package com.mycompany.myplugin`).

When a consuming web application runs [`wefter sync`](/cli/sync), the Wefter CLI copies plugin `.kt` files into the host app's `.wefter/native/android` project tree and automatically replaces the `package <name>` header line with the host application's package namespace (e.g. `package com.example.myapp`).

<Callout type="info">
  **Flexible Package Declarations**: You are free to declare any package name in
  your plugin's `.kt` files. `wefter sync` dynamically detects and rewrites the
  package header at build/sync time.
</Callout>

---

## iOS Source Copying Mechanics

Unlike Android's namespace rewrite step, Swift files (`ios/*.swift`) are copied verbatim into the host iOS Xcode project target (`WefterBridge`). No text substitution occurs on Swift files.

---

## Verifying the Scaffold

Immediately after scaffolding, run `wefter plugin validate` to confirm the scaffold passes validation checks:

```bash
cd secure-storage
wefter plugin validate
```
